key_insight: Asymmetric dimple roughness can generate large lift on a sphere without significantly changing mean drag by creating a pressure imbalance, nonuniform separation, and a wake-deflecting vortex pair.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a passive surface-texture strategy for steering forces on bluff bodies while preserving drag performance, useful for flow control and maneuvering applications.
method: Wall-resolved LES at Re = 100,000 on spheres with k/d = 0.004, 0.006, and 0.008
Pressure-force and Fourier decomposition to separate axisymmetric drag and non-axisymmetric lift contributions
Comparison of transition and separation behavior on dimpled versus smooth hemispheres
evidence_signal: The simulations reproduce prior experiments, showing lift comparable to peak Magnus force while the mean drag remains nearly unchanged.
watch_item: The mechanism depends on a specific roughness asymmetry and high-Reynolds-number transitional behavior, so performance may be sensitive to geometry, orientation, and operating conditions.
paper_title: Mechanisms of lift generation and drag invariance by asymmetric surface roughness on a sphere
